help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the Germans on holiday: they are among the travel champions of the world, with about thirty days of holiday a year; most of them still spend their main holiday in their own country, by the Baltic Sea or in Bavaria; abroad the favourites are Spain, Italy and Austria; and a certain Spanish island is jokingly called the seventeenth federal state. The text also explains the Strandkorb, the German beach chair, and the towel on the sun lounger at six in the morning. The facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: Woher? Wo? Wohin? with the right prepositions and cases (nach Spanien, an die Ostsee, in den Bergen, auf Mallorca, aus Deutschland) and the dative prepositions (mit dem Auto, bei der Familie, zu Hause). Read for the gist first, then find one place or number per question.
help.tips[0].title: Woher? Wo? Wohin? with places
help.tips[0].text: Wohin? (direction, accusative with in/an/auf): nach Spanien, nach Italien (countries without article); in die Berge, in die Türkei; an die Ostsee, ans Meer; auf die Insel, auf Mallorca (no article). Wo? (place, dative): in Spanien, in den Bergen, an der Ostsee, am Meer, auf der Insel, auf Mallorca, zu Hause. Woher? (origin): aus Deutschland, aus den Bergen, von der Ostsee, vom Meer, von Mallorca. Pairs to remember: an die Ostsee / an der Ostsee, in die Berge / in den Bergen.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Many go to the Baltic Sea or to the mountains; there, by the Baltic Sea and in the mountains, they stay two weeks.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Where do the tourists on Mallorca come from? Most come from Germany.
help.tips[0].check.why: Wohin? with an takes the accusative: an die Ostsee. an der Ostsee is Wo?.
help.tips[1].title: Dative prepositions on holiday
help.tips[1].text: mit, nach, bei, seit, von, zu, aus always take the dative: mit dem Auto, mit der Bahn, mit dem Flugzeug; bei der Familie, bei Freunden; nach dem Frühstück; von der Arbeit; zu Hause, zum Strand (zu dem), zur Insel (zu der); aus dem Norden. Short forms: zum, zur, vom, beim.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Most go by car, many fly by plane, and some stay at home with the family.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: After breakfast everyone goes to the beach, but the sun lounger has been taken since six o'clock.
help.tips[1].check.q: Wir fahren ____ Zug nach Italien. (der Zug)
help.tips[1].check.why: mit takes the dative; der Zug → dem Zug.
help.remember[0]: Wohin? an die Ostsee, in die Berge, nach Spanien, auf Mallorca; Wo? an der Ostsee, in den Bergen, in Spanien, auf Mallorca.
help.remember[1]: mit, nach, bei, seit, von, zu, aus + dative: mit dem Auto, bei der Familie, zum Strand.
help.exam: Short texts about travel and holidays with places and numbers are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Thirty days of holiday, a towel on the sun lounger at six in the morning and an island that Germans call their seventeenth state: read where the Germans go.
help.vocab[2].example: Das beliebteste Reiseland ist Deutschland selbst.
passageTranslation:
Germans have a lot of holiday: about thirty days a year, plus the public holidays. And they like travelling. Only the Chinese and the Americans spend more money abroad than the Germans.

Where do they go? The answer surprises many: the most popular destination is Germany itself. Almost every third German spends the main holiday in their own country. Most of all they go to the Baltic Sea, to the North Sea or to the mountains in Bavaria. By the Baltic they then sit in a Strandkorb. That is a basket of wood with a roof, for two people, against wind and sun. It exists only in Germany, since 1882.

Abroad, Spain is number one, then come Italy and Turkey, after that Austria and Greece. On Mallorca there are so many Germans that the island is called 'the seventeenth federal state'. Every year about five million Germans fly to the island. Most come from North Rhine-Westphalia and from Bavaria.

How do they travel? Most go by car, especially to Italy and Austria. By plane they fly to Spain and Turkey. Only a few go by train.

And there is a famous cliché: German tourists get up at six in the hotel and put a towel on the sun lounger by the pool. Then they go back to sleep. The lounger is now taken. Is it true? Ask at the pool.
questions[0].explanation: "Die Deutschen haben viel Urlaub: etwa dreißig Tage im Jahr, plus die Feiertage."
questions[0].questionTranslation: About how much holiday do Germans have?
questions[0].optionsTranslation[1]: thirty days a year plus public holidays
questions[0].optionsTranslation[3]: six weeks in summer plus all public holidays in winter
questions[1].explanation: "Das beliebteste Reiseland ist Deutschland selbst. Fast jeder dritte Deutsche macht den großen Urlaub im eigenen Land."
questions[1].questionTranslation: What is the Germans' most popular destination?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[0]: Spain, especially the island of Mallorca
questions[2].explanation: fahren + direction = Wohin?; an + accusative: an die Ostsee. Wo? would be an der Ostsee.
questions[2].questionTranslation: 'Most of all they go to the Baltic Sea.' Which question fits, and which case is it?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: Wo? dative, because they stay there
questions[3].explanation: "Das ist ein Korb aus Holz mit einem Dach, für zwei Personen, gegen Wind und Sonne. Ihn gibt es nur in Deutschland, seit 1882."
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: a wooden basket with a roof, for two people, against wind and sun
questions[3].optionsTranslation[3]: a small hotel right on the beach with a view of the sea
questions[4].explanation: "Im Ausland ist Spanien die Nummer eins, dann kommen Italien und die Türkei …"
questions[4].questionTranslation: Which country abroad is number one?
questions[5].explanation: "Auf Mallorca sind die Deutschen so viele, dass man die Insel ‚das siebzehnte Bundesland‘ nennt." Germany has sixteen states.
questions[5].questionTranslation: Why is Mallorca called 'the seventeenth federal state'?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: because the island has officially belonged to Germany since 1990
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: because so many Germans holiday there
questions[5].optionsTranslation[3]: because the island has seventeen towns
questions[6].explanation: "Mit dem Auto fahren die meisten, besonders nach Italien und Österreich."
questions[6].questionTranslation: How do most travel to Italy and Austria?
questions[7].explanation: "Deutsche Touristen stehen im Hotel um sechs Uhr auf und legen ein Handtuch auf die Liege am Pool. Dann gehen sie wieder schlafen."
questions[7].questionTranslation: What is the cliché about German tourists?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: They put a towel on the sun lounger at six and go back to sleep.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[2]: They swim every morning at six.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[3]: They have breakfast by the pool every morning at six and swim afterwards.
